svg.title: A Mastercard Virtual Card Token in an existing checkout form: a signed agent at the edge, a DTVC in card fields, Verifiable Intent L3a and L3b
svg.desc: Sequence diagram: A Mastercard Virtual Card Token in an existing checkout form: a signed agent at the edge, a DTVC in card fields, Verifiable Intent L3a and L3b. 8 participants: Consumer, Agent platform (registered agent), CDN or merchant edge, Mastercard key directory (location not public), Merchant checkout, Acquirer or PSP, Mastercard (Checkout Solutions, network and token service), and Issuer. 14 steps, 13 crossing a trust boundary, 8 failure branches. Based on several protocols Agent Pay developer guides (unversioned, read 2026-10-21) Verifiable Intent 0.1 (main at 356c296) (2026-04-20). Step 1: Consumer to Agent platform (registered agent): Delegate the purchase: sign Verifiable Intent L2 (specified live use not shown publicly). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Agent platform (registered agent) to CDN or merchant edge: GET product page, RFC 9421 signature with tag Agent-pay-auth. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: CDN or merchant edge to Mastercard key directory (location not public): Check tag, fields, timestamps and nonce, then fetch the agent key (directory location unknown). This step crosses a trust boundary. If A required field is missing: Blocked. If Window longer than 8 minutes or nonce seen in the last 8 minutes: Blocked. If Key not found in the directory: Mastercard's Level 1 decision table blocks the request. Step 4: CDN or merchant edge to Merchant checkout: Verify the signature, record the nonce, then forward. This step crosses a trust boundary. If No Signature-Input or no scheme tag: Sent to the merchant's non-agent bot policy. If Signature does not verify: Blocked. Step 5: Merchant checkout to Agent platform (registered agent): Checkout page with standard card fields (and a checkout_jwt, per spec). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Agent platform (registered agent) to Mastercard (Checkout Solutions, network and token service): Request a Virtual Card Token checkout for the merchant domain. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Mastercard (Checkout Solutions, network and token service) to Agent platform (registered agent): Return the token, its expiry and a one-time DTVC. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 8: Agent platform (registered agent) to Agent platform (registered agent): Sign L3a and L3b linked by checkout_hash (specified live use not shown publicly). Step 9: Agent platform (registered agent) to CDN or merchant edge: POST the card form: token, expiry and DTVC in standard fields. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 10: Agent platform (registered agent) to Merchant checkout: Present L1, L2 and L3b to the merchant (specified transport not defined). This step crosses a trust boundary. If checkout_hash differs from the merchant's own checkout_jwt hash: Checkout-payment mismatch the merchant rejects the order. Step 11: Merchant checkout to Acquirer or PSP: Submit the authorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Acquirer or PSP to Mastercard (Checkout Solutions, network and token service): Authorization: detokenize, validate the DTVC, check L3a (per spec). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The DTVC fails or was already used: Validation fails the authorization tells the issuer whether DTVC validation was performed, and the response code is not published. If The amount exceeds the L2 amount_range or budget: Per spec the network rejects the chain no published response code. Step 13: Mastercard (Checkout Solutions, network and token service) to Issuer: Route with the DTVC validation indicator. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 14: Issuer to Merchant checkout: Approve or decline, then disputes under standard rules. This step crosses a trust boundary.
